topics.title: Coursework
topics.summary: No blanket ban on AI in ordinary courses was found. According to Fudan's official announcement, the January 2026 teaching guide allows AI for supporting steps such as language polishing and structural suggestions but not for core academic work, and expects course syllabi to set AI conditions. The stricter undergraduate-thesis rule applies to course, term and exam papers only where no specific rule exists ('may refer to').
topics.scope: Fudan rule on AI tools in undergraduate theses (24 Sep 2024, trial; reproduced in a college's 2024 thesis rules); Fudan official news on the Generative AI Teaching Application Guide 1.0 (Jan 2026; guide text itself not reviewed); Student Disciplinary and Student Appeals Regulations; Information Office AI Service Hall notice. Institution audit remains PARTIAL.

claims.text: On 12 January 2026 Fudan launched the AI3A education co-creation platform and published the Generative AI Education and Teaching Application Guide 1.0, with 11 annexes such as an AI use declaration template and reference syllabus clauses. According to Fudan's official announcement, the guide allows AI for supporting steps such as language polishing and structural suggestions but not to replace core academic work such as research conception, theory building and data analysis, and judges integrity mainly on honest disclosure and process records. The guide's full text sits on the AI3A platform and was not independently reviewed; it is teaching guidance and does not by itself override the stricter undergraduate-thesis rule.

topics.title: Disclosure
topics.summary: For undergraduate theses, any AI use must be disclosed in the thesis commitment form: tool name and version, time and purpose, what the AI produced, where it was used, plus keeping pre-AI materials for inspection. The 2026 teaching guide, as reported, judges integrity mainly on honest disclosure and process records.
topics.scope: Fudan rule on AI tools in undergraduate theses (24 Sep 2024, trial; reproduced in a college's 2024 thesis rules); Fudan official news on the Generative AI Teaching Application Guide 1.0 (Jan 2026; guide text itself not reviewed); Student Disciplinary and Student Appeals Regulations; Information Office AI Service Hall notice. Institution audit remains PARTIAL.

claims.text: When AI tools are used in a Fudan undergraduate thesis, the thesis commitment form must disclose the tool name and version, time and specific purpose of use, the content or suggestions the AI produced, and the parts of the thesis where it was used; students must keep the relevant pre-AI materials for inspection by the supervisor or reviewers. The author bears final responsibility and AI cannot be listed as an author.

topics.summary: Undergraduate theses involving confidential content may not use any AI tool or upload any data or images to AI platforms. No broader university AI data rule was found in the reviewed sources; the AI Service Hall states it uses a locally deployed model to protect data (not independently verified).
topics.scope: Fudan rule on AI tools in undergraduate theses (24 Sep 2024, trial; reproduced in a college's 2024 thesis rules); Fudan official news on the Generative AI Teaching Application Guide 1.0 (Jan 2026; guide text itself not reviewed); Student Disciplinary and Student Appeals Regulations; Information Office AI Service Hall notice. claims.text: The same Fudan undergraduate-thesis rule (Article 4) prohibits AI in six areas: research design and data analysis; generating or altering original data (unless AI itself is the research topic); generating or altering original result images and key illustrations (unless a reproducible AI method is part of the design and explained in the methods); directly generating thesis text or acknowledgements, including AI language polishing and translation; use of AI by defence committee members or reviewers to evaluate the thesis; and any AI use or upload for theses involving confidential content.

additionalTopics.title: Academic integrity & procedures
additionalTopics.summary: In undergraduate theses AI may only assist (with supervisor consent) with literature search, chart suggestions, non-innovative code and reference formatting, and is banned for research design, data, key figures, writing text, language polishing and translation. Breaches are handled by seriousness, from the thesis grade or barring the defence to discipline and degree consequences only where misconduct is found. Disciplinary decisions can be appealed to the University Student Appeals Committee within 10 days, then to the Shanghai Municipal Education Commission within 15 days.
additionalTopics.scope: Fudan rule on AI tools in undergraduate theses (24 Sep 2024, trial; reproduced in a college's 2024 thesis rules); Fudan official news on the Generative AI Teaching Application Guide 1.0 (Jan 2026; guide text itself not reviewed); Student Disciplinary and Student Appeals Regulations; Information Office AI Service Hall notice. Institution audit remains PARTIAL.

claims.text: Fudan's formal rule on AI tools in undergraduate theses (adopted by the Academic Affairs Office on 24 September 2024, trial) allows AI use only with the supervisor's consent and only where AI output does not affect assessment of the student's own innovative ability, in four areas: literature search and management (verifying references), suggesting chart types and auxiliary charting (not generating or altering original data or key research figures), coding and method screening where the method is not the thesis's innovation (all code and methods must be reviewed and tested by the author), and reference formatting (with checking). This rule is specific to undergraduate theses; it is not a rule for all courses or for graduate theses.

claims.text: Under Fudan's Student Disciplinary Regulations (2017, amended 2019), students must be informed of their right to state their case and defend themselves before a sanction. A student who disagrees with a disciplinary decision may appeal to the University Student Appeals Committee within ten days (not working days) of service of the decision; the committee normally concludes within fifteen days (extendable by fifteen), and a student who disagrees with the review decision may appeal to the Shanghai Municipal Education Commission within fifteen days of its service (Student Appeals Regulations, effective 1 September 2017). A teacher's request to redo or supplement an assessment is not automatically a disciplinary decision.
